correctness.rationale: In the n-regular complete prism a first force needs the forcing vertex and n−1 of its neighbors, so no set smaller than n works. At equality this determines the full layer or a mixed set indexed by a missing layer index a and an included opposite index b, with a≠b. In the latter case A_b first fills A_a; a full layer forces across the matching. One exchange within a mixed family changes exactly one index; the difference of at least two in layer occupancies forbids an exchange between the two families for n≥4. The full layer jumps to all mixed states on its side but cannot slide to any, since that exchange replaces A_a with B_b for a≠b. Within a mixed family both kinds of coordinate changes are slides inside a clique. In its line graph, disjoint coordinate pairs have an intermediate state formed by a cross-coordinate pair unless the target reverses both indices. For reversals any shortest path alternates coordinate changes across three steps, with two choices of first coordinate and n−2 spare indices. This gives degree 2(n−2), one antipode, distance-two shell (n−1)(n−2), and by halving ordered pairs gives the stated totals and polynomial. The two cones are noncomplete and have a hub, hence radius one and diameter two. This proof does not depend on finite experiments.
residual_risks: No claim for n=3; the layer-count obstruction there no longer rules out cross-family jumps. Recorded verifier outputs were not independently rerun.

value.rationale: For the same minimum-state space, replacing jumps by actual host-edge slides sends each universal hub to an isolated state and gives an exact, uniform routing obstruction inside the remaining components. This provides reachability and optimal route counts for a natural forcing model, information not furnished by static enumeration; the component edge counts alone are routine consequences and not the reason for passing.
residual_risks: Value is for these two minimum-state reconfiguration rules on complete prisms, not a general reachability theorem for zero forcing.
